science.title: Why summer is hotter
science.description: "Why is summer hotter and winter colder? Many people believe seasons occur because Earth is closer to the Sun in summer and farther away in winter. This video explains why that belief is incorrect. In this video, we explore how Earth’s 23.5-degree axial tilt affects the angle of sunlight and the length of daylight throughout the year. When sunlight strikes Earth at different angles, the amount of solar energy absorbed changes, causing seasonal temperature variations. You will learn why Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January and farthest in July, why seasons are opposite in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, and how Earth’s tilt—not distance—creates summer and winter."
